newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to start second half of 96/97 firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to start second half of 96/97 firmer.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to hold a firm tone on Tuesday, the start of the second half of the 1996/97 financial year. But gains may be limited because the Nikkei average has rallied for five consecutive trading days, brokers said.
On Monday, the key 225-share Nikkei average finished up 9.38 points or 0.04 percent at 21,556.40. Its September futures gained 70 points to close at 21,570.
"Stock prices may slow rises after five days of gains, but the outer environment is favourable," said Hiroshi Morimoto, general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Morimoto said blue-chip issues, particularly automobile and high-technology shares, were likely to benefit from the yen's weakening against the dollar.
The dollar continued its bull run overnight in New York and reached a 32-month high of 111.68 yen. The U.S. currency stood at around 111.35 yen in early Asia trading on Tuesday.

Brokers also said shares in the real estate sector were expected to remain firmer towards the general election on October 20 on expectations of a review of the land tax system and new policies of liquidating land.
But the Nikkei average may not extend gains sharply unless trading volume grows to 400 million to 500 million shares, Daiwa's Morimoto said.
Trading volume was light on Monday at about 268 million shares.
